before.title: 1.4 Turbo (A14NET) Timing Chain Stretch
before.description: The A14NET 1.4 turbo engine in Astra J/K, Corsa D/E, Mokka A, and Adam can suffer timing chain stretch typically between 80,000-140,000 km. before.title: Astra H Ignition Barrel / Steering Column Lock Jamming (Key Won't Turn)
before.description: A widespread Astra H (2004-2010) failure documented across UK and German owner communities: the ignition barrel and mechanical steering column lock jam, so the key cannot be turned and the car will not start. Two failure modes are documented: a small pin on the back of the lock barrel wears a channel into its housing and jams, and a spring-loaded plastic plunger (the key-in-ignition detector) sticks due to accumulated grime, so the lock no longer registers the key. The steering lock can also bind against steering pre-load — many breakdown call-outs are resolved simply by rocking the steering wheel while turning the key. On pre-2008 cars, the related CIM (Column Integration Module) had software/hardware faults causing no-start and steering lock errors, which Opel addressed with updated software from model year 2008.
before.solution: If stranded, firmly rock the steering wheel left-right while gently turning the key to unload the lock bolt — this resolves many cases. Penetrating oil or electrical contact cleaner into the barrel can temporarily free a sticking plunger, but the fault typically returns; the lasting fix is replacing the ignition lock barrel (an auto locksmith can often code it to the existing key, which is cheaper than a dealer barrel + new keys). If the fault is electronic (no-start with steering lock error messages, pre-2008 cars), have the CIM software updated or the CIM replaced and coded by a dealer or specialist.
symptoms: Key will not turn in the ignition
Steering lock will not release
Intermittent no-start that improves after wiggling the steering wheel
Key turns but car does not recognize it
Radio stays on after key removal

before.title: Astra J Electronic Parking Brake Faults and Hill-Start Assist Rollback Recall (15-R-058)
before.description: Two related problems affect the Astra J's electronic parking brake (EPB). First, an official recall: in July 2015 Opel recalled 136,830 Astra J, Cascada and Zafira Tourer vehicles in Germany (model years 2010-2015, manual transmission with EPB and hill-start assist) under campaign 15-R-058 because a software error in the hill-start assist could create the false impression of an engaged parking brake, allowing the car to roll away on a slope. Second, owner forums (MOTOR-TALK, astra-j.de) document recurring EPB hardware faults outside the recall: a failing centre-console EPB switch (a known cheap culprit, ~EUR 20 part), seized rear caliper actuators/cables, and in worse cases a failed EPB control module that is labour-intensive to replace. Symptoms range from a 'parking brake fault' warning to the brake refusing to apply or release, immobilising the car.
before.solution: First, check with an Opel dealer whether recall 15-R-058 (hill-start assist software update, ~30 minutes of work, free of charge) was performed on the vehicle. For EPB faults: read fault codes before replacing parts. Test the console switch first (inexpensive and a frequent cause); if voltage reaches the switch and bridging the connector actuates the motors, replace the switch. Otherwise inspect rear caliper actuators and cables for seizure — seized rear calipers typically need replacement in pairs. A defective EPB control module is the most expensive outcome. Always park in gear on slopes until the system is repaired.
symptoms: Parking brake fault message on the dash
Electronic handbrake will not release
Electronic handbrake will not apply
Car rolls back on a hill despite hill-start assist
Grinding or squeaking from rear brakes
EPB switch unresponsive

before.title: Astra K 1.6 CDTI "Whisper Diesel" EGR Cooler Internal Leak and DPF Clogging
before.description: The 1.6 CDTI (B16DTH/B16DTE) "Whisper Diesel" in the Astra K suffers from a well-documented EGR cooler failure: the cooler's internal sleeve cracks, letting coolant leak into the intake/exhaust tract. Owners report white smoke at start-up, unexplained coolant loss with no visible external leak, and exhaust smell inside the cabin. UK owners on Astra K Forums report a cluster of EGR and DPF failures, several after the diesel emissions software update, with code P0401 (insufficient EGR flow) commonly logged. The same engine is also prone to DPF clogging on short-trip use and to injection-quantity drift on individual injectors, compounding rough running. German forums (astra-k-forum.de) and German troubleshooting sites document identical failures, making this a cross-market consensus issue for 2015-2019 diesel Astra K models.
before.solution: Pressure-test the cooling system and inspect the EGR cooler for internal leakage; check for coolant residue in the intake tract. Vauxhall/Opel sells the complete EGR cooler/valve assembly (around GBP 800-1000 in parts), but the cracked cooler sleeve alone is available as a separate part for roughly GBP 80 plus about an hour of labour, so insist on a sleeve-level repair quote first. Clean or force-regenerate the DPF if short-trip clogging is present, and have injector quantity corrections read out; replace and code any injector outside tolerance. Avoid sustained short-trip driving with this engine.
symptoms: White smoke from exhaust at cold start
Coolant level drops with no visible leak
Exhaust smell inside the cabin
Check engine light with code P0401
Frequent DPF regenerations or DPF warning
Rough running or jerking at light load

before.title: Astra K 1.6 Diesel Brake Fluid Contamination Recall — Reduced Braking Performance (18-C-120)
before.description: Official safety recall affecting Astra K 1.6-litre diesel models with manual transmission built from 23 March 2015 to 15 August 2018 (over 37,000 vehicles in the UK alone, plus German-market cars; campaign 18-C-120). A faulty seal in the clutch slave cylinder can degrade and contaminate the shared hydraulic fluid, leading to reduced braking power and longer brake pedal travel during slow, sustained pedal application. The remedy was staged in two steps: an immediate brake-system check and complete replacement of the brake/clutch hydraulic fluid, followed — once parts were available — by replacement of the defective cylinder components, a job of up to seven hours. The recall was reported by the German trade press (kfz-betrieb) in January 2019 and discussed by affected owners in German Astra K forums.
before.solution: Check the vehicle's recall status with an Opel/Vauxhall dealer using the VIN and have campaign 18-C-120 completed free of charge — both stages: the brake/clutch fluid flush and, where required, the component replacement. On any used Astra K 1.6 diesel manual from this build window, confirm recall completion before purchase. If the brake pedal feels long or braking effort has increased on an unrepaired car, stop driving it and have the hydraulic system inspected immediately.
symptoms: Longer brake pedal travel than normal
Reduced braking power during slow, constant pedal application
Spongy brake pedal feel
Discoloured or contaminated brake fluid
Clutch pedal feel changes accompanying brake symptoms

before.title: Astra L 1.2 Turbo (PureTech) Wet Timing Belt Premature Degradation
before.description: The Astra L's 1.2 Direct Injection Turbo three-cylinder (PSA/Stellantis PureTech EB2 family) uses a timing belt that runs inside the engine oil ("wet belt"). German automotive press (AUTO BILD, auto motor und sport) and Astra owner forums document the belt swelling, cracking and shedding material long before the official 100,000 km / 6-year interval. Shed belt particles clog the oil pick-up strainer, collapsing oil pressure; in the worst case the belt fails entirely and pistons hit valves, destroying the engine. Oil condition is the trigger: fuel dilution from short trips, aged oil, wrong oil spec or stretched service intervals chemically attack the belt. Stellantis responded with a reinforced belt in production from 2022, goodwill coverage of belt-related damage up to 175,000 km / 10 years under conditions (documented service history), and a switch to a timing chain on the third-generation 1.2 from 2023 — so Astra L buyers should verify per build date which timing drive their engine has.
before.solution: Verify the engine version by build date: early Astra L 1.2 Turbos (2022 into 2023 production) have the wet belt; the Gen-3 1.2 (from late 2023, including the new hybrid) uses a chain and is not affected. For wet-belt cars: use only oil meeting the exact Stellantis specification (PSA B71 2010 / 0W-20 as specified), change it strictly on or before schedule, and avoid chronic short-trip use. Have the belt inspected via the oil filler/inspection method (a low-cost belt-wear gauge exists) and replace it early at any sign of swelling or fraying, including cleaning the oil pick-up strainer. If damage occurred within 175,000 km / 10 years with full service history, claim goodwill coverage from Opel/Stellantis before paying out of pocket.
symptoms: Oil pressure warning light
Rattling or whining from the timing cover area
Engine running rough or misfiring
Black rubber debris in the oil or oil filler neck
Loss of power or engine failure

before.title: Astra H Water Pump Failure (Z16XEP Twinport / Z18XER 1.8)
before.description: Astra H (2004-2010) water pump failure is common between 60,000-130,000 km. The Z16XEP 1.6 Twinport drives its water pump from the AUX belt — leaks show first as coolant under the pulley side. The Z18XER 1.8 drives the pump from the timing belt — that pump must be replaced WITH the cambelt service. Both share plastic-impeller failure modes and often co-fail with the thermostat housing.
before.solution: Z16XEP: water pump replacement is a stand-alone job (€150-€300 incl. labor) once aux belt is off. Z18XER: do water pump AT the timing-belt service interval (~€400-€700 combined). Replace thermostat housing at the same time — same plastic-degradation issue.
symptoms: coolant loss
overheating
sweet smell under hood
temperature gauge climbing

before.title: Astra J 1.7 CDTI EGR Valve Clogging
before.description: The A17DTR/A17DTS 1.7 CDTI diesel in Astra J (2009-2015), Mokka A, and Meriva B suffers severe EGR valve carbon buildup, typically presenting between 80,000-150,000 km. Symptoms include power loss, limp mode, and rough idle. The EGR cooler can also crack, mixing coolant with intake flow.
before.solution: EGR valve clean or replacement (€400-€800 incl. labor). EGR delete is common but illegal in most markets and fails TÜV / MOT emissions tests. Walnut blasting helps the intake manifold simultaneously.
